# Resource: stripe_product

A product Stripe sells: a good or a service that prices attach to. `terraform destroy` deletes the product, or archives it with a warning when Stripe refuses because a price exists for it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_product" "gold" {
  name        = "Gold plan"
  description = "Everything in Silver, plus priority support."

  metadata = {
    tier = "gold"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `name` - (Required) The product's name, meant to be displayable to the customer.

The following arguments are optional:

* `active` - (Optional) Whether the product is currently available for purchase. Defaults to `true`. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `default_price` - (Optional) The ID of the [Price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices) object that is the default price for this product. Default: not sent. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `default_price_data` - (Optional) Data used to generate a new [Price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices) object. This Price will be set as the default price for this product. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`default_price_data`](#default_price_data) below.
* `description` - (Optional) The product's description, meant to be displayable to the customer. Use this field to optionally store a long form explanation of the product being sold for your own rendering purposes.
* `id` - (Optional) An identifier will be randomly generated by Stripe. You can optionally override this ID, but the ID must be unique across all products in your Stripe account. Changing it replaces the resource. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `images` - (Optional) A list of up to 8 URLs of images for this product, meant to be displayable to the customer. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `marketing_features` - (Optional) A list of up to 15 marketing features for this product. These are displayed in [pricing tables](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/pricing-table). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`marketing_features`](#marketing_features) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `package_dimensions` - (Optional) The dimensions of this product for shipping purposes. See [`package_dimensions`](#package_dimensions) below.
* `shippable` - (Optional) Whether this product is shipped (i.e., physical goods).
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional) An arbitrary string to be displayed on your customer's credit card or bank statement. While most banks display this information consistently, some may display it incorrectly or not at all. This may be up to 22 characters. The statement description may not include `<`, `>`, `\`, `"`, `'` characters, and will appear on your customer's statement in capital letters. Non-ASCII characters are automatically stripped. It must contain at least one letter. Only used for subscription payments.
* `tax_code` - (Optional) A [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-categories) ID.
* `tax_details` - (Optional) Tax details for this product, including the [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-codes) and an optional performance location. See [`tax_details`](#tax_details) below.
* `unit_label` - (Optional) A label that represents units of this product. When set, this will be included in customers' receipts, invoices, Checkout, and the customer portal.
* `url` - (Optional) A URL of a publicly-accessible webpage for this product.

<a id="default_price_data"></a>
### `default_price_data`

The `default_price_data` attribute supports:

* `currency` - (Required)
* `currency_options` - (Optional) See [`default_price_data.currency_options`](#default_price_data.currency_options) below.
* `custom_unit_amount` - (Optional) See [`default_price_data.custom_unit_amount`](#default_price_data.custom_unit_amount) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional)
* `recurring` - (Optional) See [`default_price_data.recurring`](#default_price_data.recurring) below.
* `tax_behavior` - (Optional) Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.
* `unit_amount` - (Optional)
* `unit_amount_decimal` - (Optional)

<a id="default_price_data.currency_options"></a>
### `default_price_data.currency_options`

The `default_price_data.currency_options` attribute is a map. Each value supports:

* `custom_unit_amount` - (Optional) See [`default_price_data.currency_options.custom_unit_amount`](#default_price_data.currency_options.custom_unit_amount) below.
* `tax_behavior` - (Optional) Possible values: `exclusive`, `inclusive`, `unspecified`.
* `tiers` - (Optional) See [`default_price_data.currency_options.tiers`](#default_price_data.currency_options.tiers) below.
* `unit_amount` - (Optional)
* `unit_amount_decimal` - (Optional)

<a id="default_price_data.currency_options.custom_unit_amount"></a>
### `default_price_data.currency_options.custom_unit_amount`

The `default_price_data.currency_options.custom_unit_amount` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - (Required)
* `maximum` - (Optional)
* `minimum` - (Optional)
* `preset` - (Optional)

<a id="default_price_data.currency_options.tiers"></a>
### `default_price_data.currency_options.tiers`

The `default_price_data.currency_options.tiers` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `flat_amount` - (Optional)
* `flat_amount_decimal` - (Optional)
* `unit_amount` - (Optional)
* `unit_amount_decimal` - (Optional)
* `up_to` - (Required)

<a id="default_price_data.custom_unit_amount"></a>
### `default_price_data.custom_unit_amount`

The `default_price_data.custom_unit_amount` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - (Required)
* `maximum` - (Optional)
* `minimum` - (Optional)
* `preset` - (Optional)

<a id="default_price_data.recurring"></a>
### `default_price_data.recurring`

The `default_price_data.recurring` attribute supports:

* `interval` - (Required) Possible values: `day`, `month`, `week`, `year`.
* `interval_count` - (Optional)

<a id="marketing_features"></a>
### `marketing_features`

The `marketing_features` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `name` - (Required) The marketing feature name. Up to 80 characters long.

<a id="package_dimensions"></a>
### `package_dimensions`

The `package_dimensions` attribute supports:

* `height` - (Required) Height, in inches.
* `length` - (Required) Length, in inches.
* `weight` - (Required) Weight, in ounces.
* `width` - (Required) Width, in inches.

<a id="tax_details"></a>
### `tax_details`

The `tax_details` attribute supports:

* `performance_location` - (Optional) The ID of a tax location with type `performance`, representing where the performance takes place.
* `tax_code` - (Optional) A [tax code](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/tax-categories) ID.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - The Stripe ID of the object.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `updated` - Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a product using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_product.gold
  id = "prod_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_product.gold
  identity = {
    id = "prod_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the product.

Using `terraform import`, import a product using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_product.gold prod_123
```

~> Stripe does not return `default_price_data`, so an imported product has it null: a configuration that sets it plans a replacement after the import.
